subject: Discovery Recap: Multi-tenancy controls & per-customer routing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Hill <marcus.hill@orbitalai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-28T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery Recap: Multi-tenancy controls & per-customer routing

Marcus — thanks again for the 45-minute call today. Quick recap of what we heard, desired outcomes, and next steps so we’re all aligned. Please reply with any corrections or additional details.

Key pain points you shared:
- Noisy tenants impacting cluster throughput and causing elevated tail latency for other customers.
- Lack of per-customer rate limits or quotas in your gateway today — all traffic is treated equally.
- Billing reconciliation is manual because usage buckets are not segmented by tenant.
- Need for tiering (free/dev vs. paid tiers) with different performance guarantees.

Current stack (as you described it):
- Self-hosted inference clusters on Kubernetes (NVIDIA H100s) behind a custom gateway.
- Custom metrics emitted to Prometheus, billing is a separate batch job.
- ~120 active tenants, 5 "VIP" customers with strict SLOs.

Success criteria for a first-phase integration:
- Per-tenant request quotas and burst limits enforced at the gateway level.
- Routing/policy capabilities to pin VIP customers to dedicated nodes or capacity pools.
- Clear per-tenant usage reporting (token counts + latency distributions) for billing and SLAs.
- Ability to define tiered performance (e.g., gold/silver/bronze) and automatic fallback policies.

Suggested next steps: 
1) We’ll draft a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones for a 6-week POC. I’ve attached a proposed multitenancy config spreadsheet and an example SOC2/SLA doc for reference.
2) Can you confirm current RPS and peak token/sec per tenant and the total number of active tenants (you mentioned ~120)?
3) Ben will follow up on commercial questions and pricing tiers. Lauren will scope technical integration details (API hooks, routing labels, metrics required).
4) Proposed follow-up: 30-minute technical sync next week (Apr 4–6 windows).

Open questions for you today:
- Which customers must be routed to isolated capacity (names or count)?
- Do you have data residency requirements for any tenants?
- Any hard SLA / latency targets for VIPs (e.g., p95 < 200ms)?

Thanks — we’ll prepare the MAP and a short implementation plan.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0124

Attachments: proposed_multitenancy_config.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), SOC2_SLA.pdf (doc stub)

From: Marcus Hill <marcus.hill@orbitalai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-28T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Multi-tenancy controls & per-customer routing

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns well. Couple of clarifications and added context: 

- Confirmed numbers: ~120 active tenants, peak concurrent tenants during a major campaign hits ~40. Average token/sec per tenant is low (~100–200 tokens/sec) but top 10 tenants spike to ~5k tokens/sec during campaigns. Total cluster peak token/sec ~120k.
- VIPs: 5 customers (names withheld here; we can share in a short NDA call) require dedicated routing and separate SLAs.
- Data residency: Two EU customers require EU-only processing. We run an EU cluster for those customers.
- SLA targets: For VIPs we want p95 generation latency < 250ms and 99.9% availability for inference endpoints during business hours.
- Billing: Prefer unit-based billing (token counts) with an exportable per-tenant CSV each day.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) Can you support tenant-level quota enforcement with burst windows (e.g., allow short bursts above quota but throttle sustained rates)?
2) Can VIPs be pinned to dedicated capacity pools with automatic fallback to shared capacity if dedicated nodes are down?
3) How granular is the usage reporting (per-request token-level vs. aggregated per-minute)?

We’re happy to proceed with the POC. Next week is good for a tech sync — Wed/Thu mornings PT preferred.

—Marcus
Marcus Hill
Head of Infrastructure | Orbital AI
marcus.hill@orbitalai.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Hill <marcus.hill@orbitalai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-28T19:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Multi-tenancy controls & per-customer routing

Marcus — great detail, thanks. Quick answers: 
- Yes, we support tenant-level quota enforcement with burst windows. Policy can be configured per-tenant: sustained rate + short burst allowance, and we expose those controls via API and Console. 
- VIP pinning: we can pin tenants to Dedicated capacity pools; we also support a configurable fallback policy that will route to compatible shared capacity if dedicated is unavailable (and we can limit failover behavior).
- Usage reporting: we provide per-request token counts in our telemetry and can aggregate to per-minute or daily exports for billing. We’ll include sample exports in the MAP.

I’ll coordinate with pricing on tiering options (dev/free, standard, pro/gold) and include an estimated cost delta for dedicated pools. Marissa — I’ll send a draft MAP and proposed SOW by EOD tomorrow. 

Marcus — can you share a redacted list of VIP tenant ids (or a count) and the EU-tenant ids for the residency requirement? We’ll treat any tenant ids you share as scoped only for POC.

Also looping Lauren to scope the integration (API hooks, expected labels/metadata on requests).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Hill <marcus.hill@orbitalai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-29T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Multi-tenancy controls & per-customer routing

On Mon, Mar 28, 2027 at 6:05 PM Marcus Hill <marcus.hill@orbitalai.com> wrote:
> Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns well. Couple of clarifications and added context: 
> 
> - Confirmed numbers: ~120 active tenants, peak concurrent tenants during a major campaign hits ~40. Average token/sec per tenant is low (~100–200 tokens/sec) but top 10 tenants spike to ~5k tokens/sec during campaigns. Total cluster peak token/sec ~120k.
> - VIPs: 5 customers (names withheld here; we can share in a short NDA call) require dedicated routing and separate SLAs.
> - Data residency: Two EU customers require EU-only processing. We run an EU cluster for those customers.
> - SLA targets: For VIPs we want p95 generation latency < 250ms and 99.9% availability for inference endpoints during business hours.

Marcus — thanks for the numbers. From a technical perspective, items we’ll scope for the POC: 
- Quota enforcement: we’ll validate token-level throttling + burst windows. We’ll propose policies as part of the POC and include a small rule set UI for the Console and API.
- Routing & pinning: we’ll demonstrate tenant pinning to a reserved capacity pool and show automatic fallback behavior (with a configurable failover threshold).
- Metrics & reporting: we’ll enable per-request telemetry ingestion and produce daily per-tenant CSV exports; we can also stream events to your existing Prometheus/Grafana stack or to a BigQuery sink.
- Residency: we’ll configure region routing rules so EU-tenant traffic only goes to EU nodes; we’ll provide a verification test plan for residency.

Prep for the tech sync: please share (before the call) a) a sample tenant id you’re comfortable sharing, b) rate profile for one spike tenant (requests/sec and tokens/request) and c) the names/ids of the 5 VIPs (or at least the count if you prefer to share later).

I’ll attach a short integration checklist and a sample policy JSON in the MAP we send tomorrow.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Attachment: integration_checklist.pdf (stub)
